paper.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
paper.paper_scope: Two Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steels — a Ti/V-free steel (M1) and a Ti/V-modified steel (M2) — are compared in solution-treated and aged (550 °C for 10/30 h) conditions to clarify how high-temperature (Ti,V)C carbides act as carbon sinks that regulate κ-carbide precipitation and thereby affect yield strength, work-hardening capacity and planar-slip deformation behavior.
paper.title: Formation of precipitates and their effects on the mechanical properties in a Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steel

Text names the solution-treated M1 steel M1-SS; it is the M1 alloy in the solution-treated condition (single-phase austenite, no precipitates).
Text names the M1 steel aged 30 h as M1-30; it shows homogeneous κ-carbide precipitation (mean radius 10.8 ± 6.2 nm, volume fraction 7.4 ± 3.4 %).
Text names the solution-treated M2 steel M2-SS; it contains intragranular (Ti,V)C carbides (average size 35.8 ± 20.1 nm) in the austenite matrix.
Text names the M2 steel aged 10 h as M2-10; κ-carbides preferentially precipitate at the edge of (Ti,V)C carbides with almost no matrix κ-carbides.
Text names the M2 steel aged 30 h as M2-30; κ-carbides still predominantly precipitate at the edge of (Ti,V)C carbides (mean radius 9.7 ± 8.5 nm, volume fraction 3.2 ± 2.8 %).

unmapped_findings: High-temperature (Ti,V)C carbides form during solution treatment (precipitation temperatures of Ti and V exceed 1000 °C), act as carbon sinks, and remain stable on aging — their size (~35.8 nm in M2-SS, ~37.1 nm in M2-30) and volume fraction (~2.4–2.3 %) do not change with aging.
Calculated stacking fault energies are ~70 mJ/m² (M1) and ~78 mJ/m² (M2), so both steels deform by planar dislocation slip; the Ti/V-modified steel shows narrower slip-band spacing.

Strengthening contributions: M1 aging strength increase is dominated by shearing of κ-carbides; in M2 the reduced κ-carbide shearing contribution is supplemented by Orowan bypassing of non-shearable (Ti,V)C carbides, raising tensile strength from 1004 MPa (Ti/V-free) to 1096 MPa (Ti/V-modified).
